The mySmartBlood application is an in vitro diagnostic medical device, intended to provide you (symptomatic end-user) the information concerning medical conditions or groups of diseases and the respective physiological or pathological states thereof, using your results of in vitro blood examination.  It operates by using the machine learning model trained on clinical cases.

You must follow three main steps to obtain results:

1. Measure all the blood parameters from our Mandatory Blood parameter List at your nearest laboratory.
2. Enter and submit the blood test results in the app.
3. Receive your mySmartBlood report including the list of most likely groups of diseases and explanations of blood parameters contributing to the results.

Benefit & Risks:

mySmartBlood is a priceless tool to guide you to the right healthcare professional and can significantly shorten your path to the final diagnosis, which is often associated with expensive diagnostic procedures. That way, the mySmartBlood enables your healthcare professional to make faster and more accurate diagnostic decisions and consequently improves your treatment and reduces your costs of the treatment.

By its inherent design, mySmartBlood does not provide information that could itself be used to confirm or discard health condition, since it always provides a list of max. 5 likely groups of diseases. By providing information in such a format, it enables the healthcare professional to naturally consider multiple options. The interpretation provided by mySmartBlood is only an information to guide you to consult the appropriate healthcare professional.

mySmartBlood is intended to be used for interpreting blood results of Caucasian adult users (older than 18 years old), both female (non-pregnant) and male, with acute and/or chronic conditions in the following fields of internal medicine (Toxicology, Endocrinology, Gastroenterology, Cardiology, Hematology, Nephrology, Pulmonology, Rheumatology).

mySmartBlood is contraindicated for use in: 

•	users below the age of 18,
•	emergency situations in general, e.g.:
        •.signs of a heart attack (severe/heavy/crushing chest pain…),
        • signs of a stroke (facial weakness, slurred speech, inability to hold both arms up…),
        • severe breathing problems,
        • any other untoward sign or symptom that may be of urgent nature or necessitate urgent or emergency care,
•	pregnancy.

Additional Information and Warnings: 

•	mySmartBlood is not a diagnostic medical device and you are not allowed and you should not make any decisions based only on the results obtained by mySmartBlood, without consulting a healthcare professional.
•	Your diagnosis shall always be determined by the responsible physician based on all available physical findings, patients’ anamneses, symptoms and results of other diagnostic tests.
•	Certain kinds of medication therapy can affect mySmartBlood outputs. When consulting with a healthcare professional, please inform them regarding this. 
•	mySmartBlood can only be used if all parameters from the Mandatory Blood Parameter List are available and the input of the blood parameters and values are correct.
•	mySmartBlood can only predict the groups of diseases that are available in its database. All the available groups of diseases are listed in the Instructions For Use, Annex II.
•	You should use mySmartBlood if you are showing any kind of medical symptoms. mySmartBlood is not designed for screening purposes.
•	Please note that obtainment of the mandatory blood parameter list measurement might be subject to additional costs by your healthcare provider or local laboratory.

ECG+ integrates with Apple Health to unleash the greatest power of your Apple Watch ECG, by analyzing and calculating heart rate variability (HRV) out of your ECG data, which is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform. Additionally, ECG+ app also provides detailed analysis of heartbeat intervals, including QT/QTc, which is an important indicator of your heart's electrical activity.

HRV refers to the variation in time between successive heartbeats, which is an indicator of the health of the autonomic nervous system. QT interval refers to the time it takes for the heart to recharge between beats, which is important for assessing cardiac health.

With HRV trends you can learn your health level changes. A up hill trend means a better physical fitness level and a down hill indicates you should pay more attention to your overall health. With QT trends you can monitor closely your QT intervals over a period of time and seek healthcare attention whenever a prolonged QT is identified automatically.

2. Calculate HRV (using RMSSD)
3. View Poincaré plot / R-R interval plot
4. HRV trends
5. Generate PDF report with HRV info
6. Send your ECG report to your healthcare provider

So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate. The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.

A learner’s guide to using point-of-care ultrasound in a clinical setting.

With ultrasound machines readily available nowadays and providing substantial information on the spot without any possible delay, POCUS is quickly becoming a standard of care. The POCUS App by dr. Ray gives users an immersive, visual guide to the most common techniques in point-of-care ultrasound and rapid bedside diagnosis and status assessments of the heart, lungs, abdomen, and vascular access. This richly illustrated mobile app focuses on standardizing techniques and improves diagnostic speed on the spot.

 - Dozens of original Images, illustrations, functional anatomy, and recommended ultrasound techniques in an easy-to-navigate format
 - Powerful search function to find exactly what you need, when you need it
 - The favorites section allows you to save techniques and instantly access them in seconds
 - Regular updates with the latest peer-reviewed information as it becomes available
 - Improve your decision-making time in diagnosis
 - Learn to assess different organ systems such as heart, lung, abdomen, and renal using POCUS
 - Master how to differentiate pathologies from normal findings using POCUS
 - Follow step-by-step instructions to put your knowledge into practice
